title: Purpose of MTF Configuration File
content: The configuration file in YAML format is essential for the MTF framework because it assigns logical channels to physical channels, defining which hardware interface is used for data reception and transmission.

title: System Communication Role
content: The configuration ensures proper communication between ECUs, the test bench, and other connected components.

title: System Representation
content: The configuration file represents the entire setup including tracers, logical channels, physical adapters, and devices, and connects them into a working system.

title: Abstraction Benefit
content: The configuration allows the same test cases to run on different setups by only updating physical channel information while keeping logical channels unchanged.

title: File Structure
content: The configuration file consists of three sections: Channels (mandatory), Mappings (mandatory), and FrameworkConfig (optional).

title: Section Order Rule
content: The order of sections in the YAML file does not affect interpretation but is kept consistent for clarity.

title: Channels Section Purpose
content: The Channels section defines logical channels which will later be mapped to physical channels.

title: Logical Channel Concept
content: A logical channel is a virtual abstraction of a physical hardware channel such as CAN, LIN, Ethernet, IO, or serial.

title: Hardware Awareness
content: Users must understand available hardware before defining channels, but only include channels relevant to the test case.

title: Naming Best Practices
content: Channel names should be meaningful and reflect the protocol or purpose, such as can_ch1 or eth_main.

title: YAML Structure
content: Channels are defined as key-value pairs where each channel name maps to a dictionary of properties.

title: Indentation Rules
content: YAML uses indentation to define hierarchy and should use spaces instead of tabs.

title: Case Sensitivity
content: All field names are case-sensitive and incorrect casing may cause parsing errors.

title: Channel Name Rules
content: Channel names must be unique, meaningful, and can include letters, numbers (not at the start), and underscores without spaces.

title: AUTOSAR Constraint
content: Channel names or aliases must match Communication Matrix names when working with AUTOSAR PDUs or signals.

title: Ethernet Listening Rules
content: MTF searches for specific Ethernet channel names like ETH-SOMEIP-SPY or patterns like CHANNEL-SPY or CHANNEL-PORT for listening.

title: Id Field
content: The Id field is mandatory, unique, and user-defined.

title: Alias Field
content: Aliases provide alternative names for a channel and are useful for reuse and database matching.

title: Type Field
content: Defines the communication type such as CAN, CANFD, LIN, FLEXRAY, ETHERNET, IO, SERIAL, PS, or BRIDGE.

title: Protocol Field
content: Specifies protocol version for complex hardware such as CAN2.0, CANFD, or LIN2.3.

title: LoggingName Field
content: Defines a custom name used in logging and tracing outputs.

title: TracerName Field
content: Links a channel to a tracer for logging incoming and outgoing data.

title: LoggingBusIndex Field
content: Optional field for IO tracing that defines a specific logging index or uses fallback rules if not defined.

title: Physical Setup Example
content: Example setup includes Ethernet connection via RJ45, two CAN buses, and one FlexRay bus.

title: Logical Channel Count
content: The setup requires 1 Ethernet channel, 4 CAN channels (2 buses with TX/RX), and 2 FlexRay channels.

title: Channel Creation Steps
content: Start with Channels keyword, then add each logical channel with Id, Type, and optional fields like Protocol and TracerName.

title: Final Channels Example
content: Final configuration includes Ethernet, CAN-FD, CAN, and FlexRay channels each with proper Id, Type, and tracer configuration.

title: Mappings Overview
content: Mappings section is used to connect logical channels (defined in Channels section) to physical hardware devices. It allows the framework to know which hardware resource to use when a logical channel is referenced in test cases. This enables reusable tests and flexible hardware configurations.

title: Mappings Section Structure
content: Mappings section starts with 'Mappings:'. Under it, each entry represents a hardware category such as CM, BTS, PCAP, PowerSupply, Serial, VirtualDevices. Each type has its own structure like Devices, Boards, Channels, Ports, or Buses.

title: Supported Device Types in Mappings
content: Mappings can include multiple device types: CM (Capture Module), BTS (Boards + EthernetConfiguration), PCAP (network adapters), Power Supplies (Genesys, Manson), Serial (Ports), VirtualDevices (Buses). Each type has specific configuration fields.

title: Capture Module Mapping Overview
content: Capture Modules (CM) are used to record communication data (CAN, LIN, FlexRay, Ethernet). Logical channels are mapped to CM hardware channels using configuration fields like Id, Type, Buses, HWChannel.

title: CM Common Fields
content: Common CM fields include: Id (last byte of IP), Type (CAN_Combo or LIN_Combo), Buses (logical channels), HWChannel (physical channel ID), OperationMode (Normal, Spy, TxOnly, RxOnly).

title: CM Operation Modes
content: OperationMode defines how the channel behaves: Normal (Tx + Rx), Spy (listen only), TxOnly (send only), RxOnly (receive only).

title: FlexRay Specific Fields
content: FlexRay mapping requires additional fields: KeySlot (slot for sync/startup), NodeType (ColdStartLeading, ColdStartFollowing, etc.), WakeUpCluster (wake-up signal support).

title: CM Mapping Setup Example
content: Example setup shows two Capture Modules communicating via CAN and FlexRay. Logical channels are defined first, then mapped to physical channels using HWChannel and FlexRay-specific fields.

title: Power Supply Mapping Overview
content: Power supplies (Genesys, Manson, Stamos) can be mapped to logical channels. Each channel represents a power output with configurable voltage and current.

title: Power Supply Common Fields
content: Common fields include ChannelName, DefaultVoltage, MaxVoltage, DefaultMaxCurrent, SamplingInterval, PortName, ContinuousMonitoringActive, KeepStatus, BitRate.

title: Genesys Power Supply Specific Fields
content: Genesys requires additional fields: CommunicationProtocol (Serial or TCP), IP, Port, Language (SCPI or GEN).

title: Power Supply Setup Example
content: Example includes Genesys (TCP/IP) and Manson (Serial COM). Logical channels are mapped to physical interfaces using IP/Port or COM/BitRate.

title: Network Adapter Mapping Overview
content: Network adapters (PCAP) are used for Ethernet communication. They can be physical or virtual and are mapped to logical channels.

title: Network Adapter Fields
content: Fields include Name, FriendlyName, Interface, BufferSize, BpfFilter, Timeout, TimeStampPrecision, ImmediateMode, SnapshotLength, PacketProcessingActive, PacketIdentificationActive.

title: Advanced Network Adapter Settings
content: Advanced options include UseDataLoggerTimeStamp, RemoveDataLoggerMetaData, DataLoggerType, DifferentHandlerForTxAndRx, TECMPPacketizationActive.

title: Network Adapter Best Practices
content: For logging only: disable PacketProcessingActive and PacketIdentificationActive, increase Timeout, disable ImmediateMode. For bus listening: enable both processing and identification.

title: Network Adapter Setup Example
content: Example shows Ethernet communication using PCAP adapters. Two logical channels are mapped: one for communication and one for logging.

title: BTS-REVO Overview
content: BTS-REVO is a device used to simulate buttons, sensors, and actuators. It can simulate voltage changes, on/off actions, and fault conditions like short to ground, short to VBAT, and open load.

title: BTS Mapping Purpose
content: Logical channels are mapped to BTS-REVO physical IO channels to control and monitor voltage, current, and signal states during testing.

title: BTS Mapping Structure
content: BTS mapping uses 'BTS-Revo' key. Under it, 'Boards' contains devices indexed by numbers. Each board contains Id and IOs, where IOs define channel configurations.

title: BTS Common Fields
content: Important fields: Id (last byte of IP), IOs (list of channels), ChannelName (logical channel), HWChannel (physical pin), MeasurementAttribute (Voltage, Current, PWM), Function (Relay, VBATSwitch, etc.).

title: BTS Optional Fields
content: Optional fields include LineContactState, GndContactState, VbatContactState, StaticChannel, InitValue, ChannelType, MeasurementConfig, PWMWindowTime.

title: BTS Subscription Config
content: SubscriptionConfig defines how measurements are reported: periodic polling or threshold-based triggers using UpperThreshold and LowerThreshold.

title: BTS Hardware Notes
content: BTS has 24 IO channels. Channel numbering starts from the connector farthest from power. Board Id is defined using rotary switch.

title: BTS Setup Example
content: Example shows simulation of short to ground, short to VBAT, and open load using multiple IO channels mapped to logical channels.

title: Serial Mapping Overview
content: Serial mapping is used to connect logical channels to physical COM ports for serial communication between devices.

title: Serial Fields
content: Serial fields include PortName, BaudRate, Parity, DataBits, StopBits, FlowControl, MessageTerminator, SeparationTimeMs, MaxReceivedDataSize.

title: Serial Message Terminator
content: MessageTerminator defines end-of-line characters like CR, LF, or both. It is used to detect message boundaries.

title: Serial Setup Example
content: Example shows two COM ports connected using null modem cable. One channel sends data (Master), the other receives (Slave).

title: HH Electrical Load Overview
content: HH Electrical Load is an external device used to simulate electrical load conditions. It supports PLI (single channel) and PMLI (multi-channel) series.

title: HH Electrical Load Fields
content: Main fields include PortName, BaudRate, Id, Type (PLI or PMLI), Channels mapping, ExternalTrigger, and VoltageProtection.

title: HH Load Mapping Structure
content: HH_Electrical_load uses Devices list. Each device has Id, PortName, Type, BitRate, and Channels mapping logical channel names to channel indexes.

title: HH Electrical Load Example
content: Example maps logical channel HH to COM19 using PLI device type with 115200 baud rate.

title: LF Reader Overview
content: LF Reader is an extension board for BTS-REVO supporting up to 3 antennas per board.

title: LF Reader Mapping Fields
content: LF Reader uses BoardId and Antennas list. Each antenna has AntennaNumber and HWChannel.

title: Relay Boards Overview
content: Relay boards are used to control electrical switches via CAN channel communication.

title: Relay Boards Fields
content: Relay mapping includes CANChannelName, Boards, Id, Relays, HWChannel, InitValue, DefaultValue, and Function.

title: HID Relay Boards
content: HIDRelayBoards map physical relay boards using ID and Relays configuration including HWChannel and default states.

title: WinpkFilter Overview
content: WinpkFilter is used for Ethernet packet filtering and manipulation using adapters and IP/MAC/VLAN rules.

title: WinpkFilter Fields
content: Key fields include AdapterFriendlyName, Type (Filter or FilterFastIO), IPMacTable, VLAN configuration, TTL, and packet settings.

title: WinpkFilter Example
content: Example defines sender and receiver Ethernet channels with IP-MAC mapping and VLAN tagging rules.

title: TUN/TAP Bridge Overview
content: TUN/TAP bridges virtual adapters with physical Ethernet adapters allowing VLAN tagging and packet manipulation.

title: TUN/TAP Structure
content: Bridge includes ETH_Bridge, PhysicalAdapter, TunTapAdapterList, InnerVlan, and OuterVlan configuration.

title: Time Synchronization (EES)
content: EES provides nanosecond-level synchronization for test bench devices using a GrandMaster configuration.

title: GrandMaster Field
content: GrandMaster defines which EES device is responsible for time synchronization in the system.

title: TE Analog Channels Overview
content: TE-Analog maps analog channels from devices like LIN and CM-sense to logical channels.

title: TE Analog Mapping Fields
content: Fields include ChannelName, HWChannel, and DeviceId to map analog signals to hardware.

title: Shelly Relay Mapping
content: Shelly relay is an Ethernet-controlled relay supporting HTTP/MQTT used for remote switching.

title: Shelly Relay Fields
content: Includes IP, Port, CommunicationProtocol, Channels, DoRestart, RestartDuration, and DurationAfterRestart.

title: FrameworkConfig Section Overview
content: The FrameworkConfig section is used to configure advanced framework behavior such as tracers, connected ECUs, service packs, publisher settings, Ethernet configuration, diagnostics, and optional channel fault injection settings.

title: Tracers Overview
content: Tracers define how data is logged from different communication channels. Each tracer is named and configured separately and linked to logical channels to record traffic such as CAN, Ethernet, or FlexRay.

title: PCAP Tracer Configuration
content: PCAP tracers are used for Ethernet packet capture. They support MultipleAdapterMode for multi-interface logging and PerformanceMode for high-speed optimized logging using buffers and burst writing.

title: PCAP Logging Modes
content: MultipleAdapterMode logs multiple network adapters into a single file, while PerformanceMode improves speed using multiple buffers, block writing, and burst configuration.

title: PCAP File and Buffer Configuration
content: PCAP FileConfig defines file extension, compression (zstd), base file name, and file rotation settings. BufferConfig controls buffer size, number of buffers, and write burst size to avoid packet loss.

title: ASCII Tracer Configuration
content: ASCII tracers log data in human-readable format. They support Hex or Decimal base formatting, timestamp configuration, internal event logging, and file rotation based on size or count.

title: ASCII Tracer Example Configuration
content: An ASCII tracer example includes Base formatting, InternalEventLogged flag, timestamp mode (Absolute or Relative), and file configuration with BaseFileName, Extension, MaxFile, and MaxFileSize.

title: Connected ECUs
content: ConnectedEcus defines the list of ECUs under test. Each name must match identifiers in database files such as ARXML, DBC, LDF, or FIBEX.

title: ServicePack Configuration
content: ServicePack groups multiple ECUs belonging to the same OEM and is used as an alternative to listing ECUs individually in ConnectedEcus.

title: Publisher Configuration
content: PublisherConfig defines how events are dispatched using SingleThreaded or MultiThreaded modes. MultiThreaded mode allows grouping channels into different processing threads.

title: Ethernet NPDU Configuration
content: NPduConfig manages VLAN tagging, IP-MAC mapping, and restrictions for Ethernet communication between ECUs, enabling controlled COM layer packet generation.

title: SomeIP Configuration
content: SomeIPConfig defines server-to-client port mappings, endpoint implementation (boost or lwip), and adapter selection for Ethernet communication using SOME/IP protocol.

title: App Layer Ports Configuration
content: AppLayerPorts defines port ranges for protocols such as NPdu, SomeIP, UDPNM, DLT, and SomeIpSD to control communication boundaries at application layer.

title: EthernetTopology Overview
content: EthernetTopology defines ECU-level network behavior including IP/MAC mapping, VLAN tagging, and protocol-based priority rules for Ethernet traffic handling.

title: ChannelToEcusMapping
content: ChannelToEcusMapping links logical Ethernet channels to ECUs, allowing the framework to route Ethernet traffic through correct physical interfaces.

title: Diagnostics Configuration
content: Diagnostics section configures ECU diagnostic sessions including protocol selection (DOIP or HSFZ), ECU IP address, tester IP, and optional network ID filtering.

title: ChannelsConfig Fault Injection
content: ChannelsConfig defines faulty channels used for injecting hardware faults such as short circuit or open wire conditions on CAN, LIN, or IO channels for testing robustness.

title: Important System Notes
content: Network protection or antivirus services should be disabled in test environments to avoid performance degradation when using hardware modules like CM, BTS, or EES systems.
